public_rationale: On the ordinary reading of substantive engagement, the characterization is contradicted. Newton examined reported setbacks at three major laboratories, possible limits of LLMs and their implications for superintelligence. Cowen acknowledged slowdown reports and explained why his outlook remained optimistic. These are direct counterexamples involving two people Marcus named. Their conclusions need not agree with Marcus to count as reckoning with the evidence. This finding does not establish that all three addressed every contamination concern or revised numerical AGI timelines.
limitations: The result depends on reading reckoning as substantive consideration, rather than agreement about how much weight setbacks deserve.
The assessment concerns the named examples, not every member of an unspecified pundit group.
The underlying technical truth of the model-setback reports is not independently adjudicated here.

our_interpretation: The ordinary factual reading is that the named commentators have not substantively addressed reported next-generation model setbacks and their implications for expectations about AI progress.
Reckoning with setbacks means considering them and explaining their implications. It does not require agreeing with Marcus or lengthening an AGI timeline.
The surrounding reference to GPT-5-level models makes GPT-5 a description of an expected generation of capability, rather than exclusively an OpenAI product name.
The target is the public commentary record available through April 7, 2025, the latest observable state before publication. No starting date is supplied, so the start remains unspecified.
The scandal characterization is an opinion. The introductory comparison with benchmark misconduct is rhetorical, not a conditional forecast.
